parsed.stack: React Native, iOS + Android. Cheap-stack speech-to-speech (~$0.008-0.015/min) for the 12-minute mock; the user's own N-400 answers typed in and fed as context so the officer asks about their real travel dates and addresses. Public USCIS content (N-400 form, 100 civics questions) so no licensing cost. Transcript scoring by a Haiku-class text pass. Consumable credits via StoreKit/Play Billing, plus a web credit purchase.
milestones: Week 1-2: N-400 data intake (the user types their own answers once) and the officer prompt that questions those specific facts.
Week 3-4: the 12-minute voice mock with interruption and one unprepared follow-up per session - the interruption behaviour is the product, a polite turn-taker is worthless here.
Week 5-6: post-mock review: transcript, the answers that contradicted the typed N-400, civics questions missed.
Week 7: hard legal framing - practice only, not legal advice, no eligibility opinions - plus a refusal path when the user asks for immigration advice.
Week 8: one free mock then credits; seed through two immigrant-services nonprofits and the r/USCIS-style communities.
parsed.riskiest_technical_assumption: That the voice model sustains an officer persona that interrupts and probes the user's own typed N-400 facts for 12 minutes without drifting into hallucinated legal or eligibility claims, which in this audience is an actively harmful failure, not a cosmetic one.
parsed.cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption: Script ten adversarial 12-minute mocks (including users who ask 'will I pass?') against the cheap stack and have an immigration paralegal read the transcripts for anything that reads as legal advice - a few hours of their time.
